mistake_content: Hardcoded wait in function - time.sleep() used inside test function instead of dynamic wait. Related to GM-001.
solution: Remove the hardcoded time.sleep(5) call in test_06 method. Replace it with a dynamic wait that checks for the actual condition needed before clicking the toggle button. Use self.driver.wait_for_object() to wait for the specific element or UI state to be ready. This makes the test more reliable and faster by waiting only as long as necessary for the actual condition to be met, rather than a fixed 5-second delay.

mistake_content: The test method 'test_04_verify_the_screen_when_the_user_clicks_on_go_back_button' is missing the TestRail case ID suffix '_C49'. The docstring references TestRail case 49, but the method name doesn't include the required '_C49' suffix. Other test methods in the same file correctly follow the naming pattern with case IDs (e.g., test_01_..._C46, test_02_..._C47, test_03_..._C48, test_05_..._C50, test_06_..._C51), making this method inconsistent.
solution: Rename the test method from 'test_04_verify_the_screen_when_the_user_clicks_on_go_back_button' to 'test_04_verify_the_screen_when_the_user_clicks_on_go_back_button_C49'. According to HPX automation naming conventions documented in Section 7.1 (STANDARD TEST FILE STRUCTURE), test methods must follow the format: 'def test_XX_<description>_C<testrail_id>(self):' where the TestRail case ID is always appended at the end of the method name with the '_C' prefix. This ensures: (1) Traceability between automated tests and TestRail test cases, (2) Consistency across the test suite for easier maintenance and reporting, (3) Proper integration with TestRail reporting tools that rely on this naming pattern to map test results. The TestRail ID must match the case number referenced in the docstring (case 49 in this instance).
